items.title: Christine Jensen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 4, 2024
items.q: I was working on Mozart binary form

ctx.x: I think it came from Bob Brookmeyer, but I said, okay I’m going to try to write a chart with no solos. And it made me realize that we depend on solos sometimes simply to have a chart that’s more than three minutes long.

It’s true. Your development has to go a different way, which is probably why it was a good thing for me to study a lot of classical theory when I was at McGill. I had to do two years of classical and it really taught me — I mean I played through it, I was playing through Beethoven sonatas, I was working on Mozart binary form, all this stuff and I think Beethoven sonatas were what probably helped me understand that form has to keep going and it’s not just variations. I mean you can add other things. So that’s kind…
